_comment: THE GUEST WIDGET DEPLOYMENT: a deployment of its own, beside the main one, where the embeddable widget, the guest issuer, the two upgrade paths and invitation links are exercised (tests/e2e/guest-widget.spec.ts and the guest deny-tests). Copy it to deploy.config.json in a checkout used only for this deployment and deploy with its own instance name, so no stack, SSM path or table is shared with the main deployment: AE_INSTANCE_NAME=ae-guest npm run deploy. Every key not listed here takes its default; deploy.config.example.json documents each one. deploy.mjs compares this file against that example and refuses only a missing key whose absence removes something (DESTRUCTIVE_IF_ABSENT in lib/config/deploy-context.ts), so the rest only warn.
_instance: Not a context key: the instance is the AE_INSTANCE_NAME environment variable (lib/stacks/agent-classification-common.ts). ae-guest gives stacks named AeGuest<Stack> and the SSM root /ae-guest.
_capabilities: widget is the frame visitors talk in; chat is where path A's visitor signs in (the guest issuer's GuestSignInUrl is the chat app); admin is the console that approves registrations and shows the guest-to-customer funnel; notifications sends path B's claim email (it needs the standard classification, below).
_profiles: guest and customer deploy only when declared: guest is the visitor's classification, and customer is where path B's claim opens its customer-engagement conversation. basic and standard are the accounts' own. Nothing a member holds reaches guest or customer: an outside classification grants only itself, and synth refuses a member classification that grants it.
_issuers: deployment: this deployment's own pool, the accounts path A binds a visit to, and the console's admins. guest: the platform's own issuer for an anonymous visitor (docs/guides/admin/GUEST-ISSUER.md); outside production a guest with no captcha uses the vendor's test keys. Its allowedOrigins names "widget-host", the sample host page (examples/widget-host/): the CDK app stands up the WidgetHost stack (a private bucket behind its own CloudFront distribution) and names that distribution's origin in the widget's frame-ancestors, read from the stack, so no domain is typed here. customers: a test-fixture pool (lib/config/test-issuers.ts) for path B's customer, whose classifications are all outside; the TestIssuer stack creates its pool on the first deploy, and the entry is trusted once its pool and audience are set from that stack's TestIssuerCustomersPoolId and TestIssuerCustomersClientId outputs.
_urls: appUrl and adminAppUrl are derived by deploy.mjs from the live distributions; leave them empty. widgetUrl, the widget frame's own origin that PersonApi admits in CORS, is derived the same way from the Widget stack's WidgetDistributionUrl output; leave it empty too. The chat app needs no setting for the widget: gen-frontend-env.mjs writes that same output into the chat app's VITE_WIDGET_ORIGIN, and path A's hand-off is taken only from that origin.
